description: Finds the times of loudness PEAKS in a sound and writes them to a text DATA file: one ascending time per line, C '%lf' format (6 decimals), no header (verified: bursts synthesized at 0.10/0.60/1.20/1.90 s -> '0.106871 / 0.601043 / 1.202993 / 1.902336' - each within ~7 ms of the true burst peak). Originally built to track syllables in speech. The sound is scanned in windowsize-ms windows; with threshold unset (or 0) an ADAPTIVE gate applies - peak windows below 1/5 of the local maximum (measured over 10 windows) are ignored; a nonzero threshold additionally discards peaks below that absolute level. Output extension is data-typed: naming it .wav is refused ('ERROR: Cannot open a textfile (pk_o.wav) with a reserved extension.'). Stereo input accepted with CHANNEL-CORRECT times (mono and stereo renders of the same material return identical times - verified). Deterministic. The duration_model 'static' is a schema placeholder - data outputs skip the audio pre-flight.
musical_use: The rhythm-harvesting half of the timefile glue: peakfind's output IS the input format of clicknew (render an audible click track at the found peaks - round-trip verified sample-tight), of retime 1's refpoints and retime 7's retempodata (re-time other material onto this sound's rhythm), and of grain reposition/rerhythm timefiles - one analysis feeds the whole event-timing toolkit. Window size is the musical zoom: large windows (100-200 ms) find only the main stresses of speech or the downbeats of a phrase; small windows (5-20 ms) catch every transient but risk confusing waveform-level amplitude ripple with the loudness envelope (excessive peaks). The adaptive default is right for material with a level arc; set an absolute threshold (0.2-0.5) to pull only the accents out of a dense texture, or when the file is too short for the adaptive gate (< 10 windows refuses without one).

windowsize.description: Window for locating successive peaks, in ms (CDP-enforced '(1.000000 to 500.000000)', Parameter[1]). Large = only major accents; very small = amplitude ripple mistaken for peaks (excessive times). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.').

threshold.description: Absolute level below which peaks are ignored (CDP-enforced '(0.000000 to 1.000000)', Parameter[2]). Unset or 0 = adaptive gate only (windows below 1/5 of the 10-window local maximum ignored). REQUIRED (> 0) for files shorter than 10 windows: 'ERROR: File too short to scan peaks without a threshold value (> 0.0) being entered.' Breakpoint refused (parameter 2).

examples.description: Harvest the main stresses of a spoken phrase.
examples.expected_use: Output .txt: one peak time per line, ascending. Copy into data/ and feed to clicknew (audible check), retime 1/7, or grain reposition.

examples.description: Accents only, from a dense texture.
examples.expected_use: Local peaks below 0.4 absolute level discarded on top of the adaptive gate.

known_issues: DATA OUTPUT (.txt): one '%lf' time per line, no header, ascending - the exact input format of clicknew's clicktimes (round-trip verified: clicks land within 2 samples of each listed time), retime 1 refpoints, retime 7 retempodata, and grain reposition timefiles. Cannot be auditioned or fed to audio inputs; duration pre-flight skipped.
Adaptive default (threshold unset/0): peak windows below 1/5 of the local max over 10 windows are ignored - quiet-passage peaks survive; an absolute threshold kills them.
Files shorter than 10 windows refuse without a positive threshold (verbatim above); with one they run (single peak verified on a 0.1 s file).
Stereo accepted, times channel-correct (verified identical mono vs stereo) - contrast retime mode 12's interleaved-sample stereo bug.
A silent input yields no peaks and an empty file (engine non-empty verification is the guard).
